conviction_note: No unpriced, company-level number decides this print. A share-count tailwind from the 10-Q cover, a provision that may normalise, and rising short interest into a stock near its 52-week low give a slight upward lean (p_up 54). Credit migration on the three NPL relationships and the softer CECL macro inputs offset part of it. abs_move 3.0% rests on the name's own 2.3% median and 16% realised vol, nudged up because this is the first bmo print in the record, so the full reaction lands inside the scored session. I did not use the 11.9% option-implied move: it comes from 33 contracts of open interest with a 66%-wide spread. The findings sum to +0.45 and the scaled number is +0.24. They agree in sign and are about the same small size.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS $1.21. Benzinga earnings page (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/FBK/earnings-forecasts, ~2026-10-01) and Earnings Whispers (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/FBK) agree; a second Benzinga forecast page shows $1.19. Revenue consensus is about $179.7-181.7M. Company guidance from the Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15226549103125504, 2026-07-13): FY NIM ex-accretion 3.70-3.80% with a couple of bp of drift per quarter, assuming one Fed hike in Q3; loan growth mid-to-high single digits; deposits at the lower end of mid-to-high single digits; banking-segment noninterest expense $325-335M; efficiency ratio about 50% by year end; tax rate about 20%. Own build: Q2 adjusted NI $58.9M; average diluted shares about 51.9M in Q2 against 49.98M outstanding at 7/31; NII +2%; provision $6-10M against $10.1M in Q2. That gives roughly $1.22-1.29 EPS, so the bar looks met to slightly beaten, and the swing is the provision.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest at the 2026-09-30 settlement was 3.0M shares, up 40.5% from 2.2M at 09-15. That is the fourth straight increase and a one-year high, about 6.1% of shares outstanding, with 3.8 days to cover (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/fbk/, read 2026-10-12). It is rising but not crowded. Skew is null in the baseline. Put/call OI is 0.43 on only 33 contracts and the ATM spread is 66% of mid, so the options say nothing usable. Tape: spot $53.48, 13.85% below the 52-week high and 5.0% above the 52-week low, 20-day -3.05%, 5-day +1.71%. The stock traded around $58 in late August (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/FBK).

findings.finding: The 10-Q cover shows 49,978,138 shares outstanding at 2026-07-31. Q2 average diluted shares were about 51.9M ($58.6M GAAP NI / $1.13 diluted EPS), after 1.55M shares (3.01%) were bought back in Q2. Flat Q2 adjusted earnings of $58.9M on about 50.1M Q3 diluted shares gives about $1.18. With NII growth on Q2's 11.6% annualised loan growth, a provision back below Q2's $10.1M, or both, the $1.21 consensus is reachable to modestly beatable.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 EPS of $1.14 against $1.15 (a slight miss) and a revenue miss still traded +3.23% over the session window. Q3 2025, a $1.07 adjusted beat against $1.03, traded +4.07%. The EPS line has been rewarded mildly or forgiven.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side models will include the buyback, so this is mostly priced. What may not be priced is the provision normalising after Q2's $10.1M spike, which was taken on three NPL relationships. If the market fully expected a clean beat, the stock would not sit 5% above its 52-week low with shorts up 40% in the last fortnight of September.
findings.independence: Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001649749/000164974926000052/a2q26pressreleasetablesfor.htm) for the buyback, Q2 provision and NI. It is a different document from the 10-Q cover but the same company data, so read it as one company-level arithmetic, not two independent sources.

findings.finding: The Q2 NIM guide (FY ex-accretion 3.70-3.80%) explicitly assumed one Fed hike in Q3 2026. The FOMC did hike 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, 12-0. FBK says it is slightly asset sensitive and that a hike helps 'to the tune of a couple million dollars'. The rate path therefore matched the guide's assumption, so the margin guide is unlikely to be cut on rates, but the Q3 benefit is only about two weeks.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NIM has been stable to rising (3.68% in Q2 2025, 3.94% in Q1 2026, 3.95% in Q2 2026). I found no clean record of the stock reacting to a NIM surprise in isolation.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the hike is public and inside the company's own guide. It matters only because a guide cut on rates is less likely. If the market feared margin pressure, regional-bank peers would have sold off on the hike, and I found no evidence that they did.
findings.independence: Q2 call transcript, rate assumption and asset-sensitivity quotes (https://www.webull.com/news/15226549103125504), a different document from the Fed release.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-24 FBK issued $125M of 6.625% fixed-to-floating subordinated notes due 2036, 'to support [FirstBank's] growth'. The prospectus says FirstBank's dividend capacity to the parent under Tennessee law 'has been substantially utilized'. That follows Q2 buybacks of 3.01% of shares and CET1 falling to 11.0% from 11.5%. Rule 4 question, what does the money buy: growth capital, corroborated by Q2 loans HFI +11.6% annualised, above the mid-to-high-single-digit guide. It also signals that holdco buyback capacity is constrained and adds about $2M a quarter of interest from Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print followed a debt raise in the record I could see.
findings.why_not_priced: The raise is public, but the call will show whether the Q3 buyback pace and loan growth continue. If the market had read the raise as a growth signal, the stock would not have drifted from about $58 to $53 since late August. If it had read it as distress, I would expect a sharper drop and wider credit spreads, and I found neither.
findings.independence: 8-K of 2026-09-24 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001649749/000121390026103052/ea0306481-8k_fbfinancial.htm), the same transaction. Loan growth from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001649749/000164974926000052/a2q26pressreleasetablesfor.htm) corroborates the growth use.

findings.finding: Credit is the swing line. Q2 NPAs rose to 1.14% of assets from 0.98% on three relationships: two individually evaluated CRE credits with about $3.5M of specific reserves, and one 'well-collateralized credit with a near-term workout plan'. The Sept 17 investor deck shows the CECL macro inputs as 'modestly softer' (Moody's national unemployment 4.5% in 3Q26 and 4.8% in 4Q26, house price index -1.5% and -2.9%). Further migration or a reserve build would keep Q3 provision at or above Q2's $10.1M. A successful workout would let NPAs fall.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print with rising NPAs and a provision jump to $10.1M from $3.0M still closed the session window +3.23%. Credit has not been punished on this name so far.
findings.why_not_priced: The direction of the workout is unknowable before the release, and the deck's macro inputs are Q2-dated. If the market expected a clean resolution, short interest would not be at a one-year high. If it expected a large loss, the stock would be below its 52-week low.
findings.independence: Q2 call commentary on the three credits (https://www.webull.com/news/15226549103125504) and the Q2 release. These are company documents, not an independent credit series. I searched Tennessee courts for borrower litigation and found nothing.

findings.finding: FINRA short interest rose 40.5% to 3.0M shares (about 6.1% of shares outstanding, 3.8 days to cover) at the 2026-09-30 settlement. That is the fourth consecutive increase and a one-year high, into a stock 5% above its 52-week low. A clean print would push shorts to cover, a supporting flow. A credit surprise would validate them.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reactions alternate in sign: +3.23, -2.30, -1.41, +4.07, -4.57, -1.97, +2.21. Median absolute 2.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is published but seldom priced into a regional bank's day-of reaction. At 6% and 3.8 days it is not crowded, so this is a small asymmetry, not a squeeze setup.
findings.independence: Stock about $58 in late August against $53.48 now (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/FBK) and the sealed baseline tape: -13.85% from the 52-week high. Same direction, different source.

findings.finding: Mortgage rates rose in early Q3: the MBA put the 30-year fixed at 6.65% in the week ending July 10, the highest since August 2025. That points to FBK's mortgage banking income (already down to $11.2M in Q2 from $12.3M in Q1) staying flat to lower in Q3. Mortgage is about 6% of revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Mortgage has drifted lower for several quarters with no visible reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and likely already in models. It is a proxy for a minor segment. The rest of the company (NII, about 85% of revenue) would have to soften too for this to matter.
findings.independence: This is a proxy; the company has not confirmed Q3 mortgage volumes. The MBA release of 2026-07-22 showed applications +1.9%, purchase +6% (https://www.mba.org/news-and-research/newsroom/news/2026/07/22/mortgage-applications-increase-in-latest-mba-weekly-survey), which partly offsets it.

Tennessee court filings or receiverships naming FirstBank as lender in 2026: none found
Any 8-K item 2.06 or other credit 8-K since Q2: none (EDGAR list since 2026-07-01 shows only the sub-debt offering, the Sept 17 deck, the July 27 KBW deck, the 10-Q and Form 4s)
Quarter-to-date data in the Sept 17 investor deck and the sub-debt prospectus: none after 2026-06-30, and no Recent Developments section
FBK-specific news or downgrades explaining the slide from about $58 (late August) to $53.48: none found
Regional-bank sector stress in October 2026 (KRE): results were October 2025 stories, nothing current
Insider Form 4s on 2026-10-08: tax withholding on RSU vesting (code F), not open-market trades

baseline_tension: The slight upward lean runs against the 20-day drift (-3%) and the 40% short build, but agrees with the stock sitting near its 52-week low. There is no usable skew to agree or disagree with. Because the lean rests on arithmetic and positioning, not an unpriced number, p_up stays close to 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 4 (financing is a question): the sub-debt raise funds loan growth that the Q2 balance sheet corroborates, so its size went from -0.2 to 0.0, with the buyback-capacity constraint kept in the range
Rule 6 (inside the guide): the Fed hike was the guide's own assumption, so the rate finding went from +0.3 to +0.15
Rule 5 (proxy smaller): the CECL macro-input finding rests on Q2-dated inputs and the credit swing is unknowable, so it went from -0.3 to -0.2; the mortgage proxy stays small at -0.1
Rule 7: short interest checked before any negative (6.1%, 3.8 days, not crowded); the negatives were left small
Rule 1: reaction history shows beats and misses alike rewarded mildly, so the reaction is sized on the 2.3% median and p_up stays at 54
